study.title: The effects of laser acupuncture dosage at PC6 (Neiguan) on brain reactivity: a pilot resting-state fMRI study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled pilot study with 1 control group and 2 experimental groups, each group comprising varying ED of LA; between-subject design with pre/post resting-state fMRI
study.randomization: Random assignment using a random number table generated by Excel (Microsoft Inc., United States)
study.population: Healthy male and female adults, postmenopausal female participants excluded, aged 18 to 55 years with BMI ranging from 18.5 to 24 kg/m2
study.inclusion_criteria: Healthy male and female participants between the ages of 18 to 55 years with a body mass index (BMI) ranging from 18.5 to 24 kg/m2; postmenopausal female participants excluded
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) subjects with chronic diseases such as coronary artery disease, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, and history of cancer; (2) subjects experiencing recent carpal tunnel syndrome or similar symptoms; (3) subjects with functional or organic diseases related to the CNS; (4) subjects unable to follow instructions or comply with study requirements; (5) pregnant women or subjects with metal implants or pacemakers; (6) subjects who had taken nerve activity-inhibiting medications such as psychiatric medications or analgesics within the past 3 months; and (7) subjects with open wounds or scar tissue around the PC6 area that may interfere with the LA intervention

conditions.condition_label_exact: Laser Acupuncture 0 mW, 20 s, Energy Density 0 J/cm2
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: This is a laser acupuncture sham using the same device set to 0 mW output power, meaning no energy is delivered to tissue. Although the device makes physical contact with the skin (contact application), a non-penetrating laser at 0 mW delivers no photonic energy and causes no tissue engagement beyond superficial contact pressure. However, the defining feature here is that the 'active' comparator is also non-penetrating laser light — the sham is distinguished by zero energy output. Since the device emits nothing, this functions effectively as a no-treatment/mock device condition. Given the contact element, this sits at the boundary of Level 3 and Level 4; however, because the laser is explicitly off (0 mW, 0 J/cm²) and the sham is defined by the absence of any physical or energetic tissue interaction beyond passive touch, it is best classified as Level 4 (no meaningful tissue engagement), consistent with 'mock laser' classification conventions in the literature.

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: SIGNA Architect AIR Edition, GE healthcare, Chicago, IL, United States
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Ascending interleaved echo-planar imaging (EPI) sequence for resting-state fMRI; 3-dimensional spoiled gradient echo sequence for structural scan
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: matrix=64×64; field of view=224×224 mm2; slice number=40; slice thickness=3.5 mm (resting-state fMRI); matrix=224×224×170; field of view=224×224×170 mm3 (structural)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 200 continuous whole-brain scans, each lasting 2.5 s, total duration: 8 min and 40 s (500 s); structural: approximately 5 min
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Data Processing Assistant for Resting-State fMRI (DPARSF, State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Neuroscience and Learning, Beijing Normal University, China); Matlab 2021b (Mathworks Inc., Sherborn, MA, United States)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Three-dimensional Gaussian kernel (8-mm full width at half maximum)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Slice acquisition times correction and realignment to minimize effects of head movement; six head movement parameters regressed out
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: Global mean signal regressed out; also white matter signals and cerebrospinal fluid signals regressed out
statistical_thresholds_exact: Family-wise error rate corrected cluster p<0.05 (the cluster forming threshold is in uncorrected voxel p<0.005)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Family-wise error rate corrected cluster p<0.05 (cluster forming threshold: uncorrected voxel p<0.005)

extraction_notes.note: Blinding of participants, assessors, and practitioners is not explicitly described. It is unclear whether participants were blinded to their group assignment. The sham (0 J/cm2) device appears identical in application to the active devices, but participant awareness of group assignment is not reported.
Deqi/sensory response during laser acupuncture was not assessed or reported. Laser acupuncture is described as non-invasive, painless, and non-thermal; no deqi sensation instrument was used.
Expectancy, credibility, and treatment blinding/credibility assessments are not mentioned in the paper.

Coordinate space (MNI or Talairach) is not explicitly stated in the paper. Use of SPM12 with EPI template normalization strongly suggests MNI space, but this is an inference and not confirmed in the text.

Table 4 header in the PDF contains a split across rows that makes some BA and ROI labeling ambiguous. The mapping of 'None Significant' to the RVLM Set 2 vs Set 3 Pre > Post comparison and 'None Significant' to DMV Pre < Post comparison was inferred from the table layout; verified against text description.

In Table 4, the Brodmann area for the right mid/inf frontal gyrus in the RVLM Set 2 vs Set 3 row is listed as '--/45', which may indicate that the BA for the first part was not determined. Extracted as 'not reported (listed as --/45 in table)'.

The paper states the figure caption for Figure 2A as 'FC enhanced in inferior part of orbitalfrontal cortex' - the typo 'orbitalfrontal' appears in the caption but 'orbitofrontal' is used in the text. The Table 4 does not list a separate coordinate row for this finding (RVLM R Set 1 vs Set 3 Pre < Post only lists Sup. Front. Gyrus, not OFC). The OFC finding is described in the text and Figure 2A caption. It is possible the OFC result from Figure 2A is contained within the 'R Sup. Front. Gyrus' cluster in Table 4, or it was figure-only. Extracted as a separate narrative result (c25).

The n_analyzed values for individual contrast entries were inferred based on the arm sizes (Set 1=16, Set 2=18, Set 3=17). For between-group comparisons, the sum of the two groups was used. These are inferred, not explicitly stated per contrast.
Blood pressure was not measured; explicitly acknowledged by authors as a limitation.
Correlation analysis timepoint for HRV-FC correlations is not specified. It is unclear whether correlations were performed on post-intervention FC maps or change scores.

The structural MRI scan parameters include flip angle=12 degrees, which the paper reports but does not provide for the resting-state EPI sequence separately in that field (EPI flip angle=90 degrees is given). Both are preserved in the neuroimaging_methods field.
Adverse events are not systematically reported. The paper only mentions that the experimental process would suspend in the event of subject discomfort; no specific adverse events are documented.

The paper describes 'Two 500-s resting-state fMRI scans were acquired' in the abstract, but the methods section specifies '200 continuous whole-brain scans, each lasting 2.5 s, total duration: 8 min and 40 s'. 200 × 2.5 s = 500 s, which is consistent; however the paper also says '8 min and 40 s' which is 520 s. This minor inconsistency is noted.

Table 5 and Table 6 list '0 J/cm2 group exhibited no significant correlation' and '0 J/cm2 still exhibited no significant correlation' but no rows for Set 1 are in these tables. This is consistent with no significant findings for the control group.
